sub_unit_name: Cement: Portland cement, its composition, setting and hardening

content.title: Portland Cement
content.description: Portland cement is a hydraulic cement obtained by grinding clinker with a small quantity of gypsum. It hardens by chemical reaction with water and is the most widely used construction material.

content.content: Ordinary Portland Cement (OPC) is manufactured from limestone and clay. It develops strength by hydration reactions and is extensively used in buildings, bridges, dams, roads, and other civil engineering structures.

content.title: Engineering Importance
content.content: Portland cement is the backbone of modern construction due to its high strength, durability, and resistance to weathering.

content.title: Manufacture and Use of Portland Cement

content.content: The main raw materials used in manufacturing Portland cement are limestone (CaCO₃) and clay. Small quantities of iron oxide, silica, alumina, and gypsum are also added to obtain the desired composition.

items.question: Tricalcium Silicate (C₃S)
items.answer: Develops early strength and releases more heat during hydration.

items.question: Dicalcium Silicate (C₂S)
items.answer: Develops strength slowly and improves durability.

items.question: Tricalcium Aluminate (C₃A)
items.answer: Accelerates initial setting but reduces sulphate resistance.

items.question: Tetracalcium Aluminoferrite (C₄AF)
items.answer: Acts as a flux during manufacture and contributes to hardness.

items.question: Gypsum
items.answer: Prevents flash setting by controlling the hydration of C₃A.

content.content: Setting is the process by which cement paste loses its plasticity after mixing with water and becomes rigid due to hydration reactions. Initial setting allows placing of concrete, while final setting makes the paste hard.

Hardening is the gradual development of strength after the cement has set. It occurs due to continuous hydration of calcium silicates, resulting in the formation of strong calcium silicate hydrate (C-S-H) gel.

items.question: Buildings
items.answer: Construction of residential and commercial buildings.

items.question: Roads and Bridges
items.answer: Used in highways, flyovers, and bridges.

items.question: Dams
items.answer: Construction of water storage and hydroelectric projects.

items.question: Precast Structures
items.answer: Manufacture of pipes, poles, and concrete blocks.

content.title: Exam Tip
content.content: Remember the composition of Portland cement, the functions of C₃S, C₂S, C₃A, C₄AF, the role of gypsum, and the difference between setting and hardening.

content.title: Quick Revision
points: Portland cement is a hydraulic cement.
Main raw materials are limestone and clay.
Major compounds are C₃S, C₂S, C₃A, and C₄AF.
Setting is the loss of plasticity.
Hardening is the gradual gain in strength.
C₃S gives early strength, while C₂S gives long-term strength.
Portland cement is widely used in construction.
